name: AgentComputer

modes.label: On-demand
modes.note: Pricing page: usage-based, CPU Time $0.07/CPU-h, Memory $0.04375/GB-h. Whether memory is billed on allocation or on use is not published (ram_basis null; engine then bills allocation, the conservative case).

modes.label: macOS QEMU/KVM on-demand
modes.note: Pricing page publishes one product-wide PAYG table but no macOS exception or selectable CPU count. Default macOS is 4 GiB RAM and a 64 GiB guest disk. Linux-only exec, file operations, mounts, published ports, resize and snapshots are unavailable on macOS.

plans.name: Pay as you go
plans.note: Unknown limits are not promises of unlimited capacity.

plans.name: Enterprise
plans.note: Unknown limits are not promises of unlimited capacity.

features.ip_note: Egress/IP and proxy options not documented.

caveats: Public PAYG pricing says actual resource usage and CPU Time: $0.07/CPU-hour, RAM $0.04375/GB-hour; hot running storage $0.000683/GB-hour, cold stopped storage $0.000027/GB-hour. Exact observed-versus-reserved RAM and CPU minimums unverified.

Features set to null were not verified. No sandbox was purchased or tested; feature/performance statements are documentation claims. Null maximums are unknown unless a cited note explicitly states unlimited.
A complete monthly bill requires known snapshot/egress/plan limits; do not silently treat missing ancillary charges as free.
Storage: hot $0.000683/GB-h while running (=$0.4986/GiB-month), cold $0.000027/GB-h while stopped (=$0.0197/GiB-month, modelled as snapshot_gib_month) per agentcomputer.ai/pricing 2026-09-28.
Memory billing basis (allocated vs used) not published; priced on allocation. Sprites-style active-RAM billing would cut memory cost ~5-8x.

Docs (agentcomputer.ai/docs, 2026-09-28): default image "pre-configured with browser access, SSH"; VNC via computer open --vnc; up to 64 GiB RAM and 250 GiB storage subject to host capacity. Egress price not published.

audit_2026_09_29.source: checked against the provider's live pricing and docs pages

snapshot_on_demand.quote: POST	/v1/computers/<id>/snapshots	Create a snapshot. ... POST	/v1/snapshots/<snapshotId>/restore	Restore a snapshot into a new computer.
snapshot_on_demand.note: CLI 'computer snapshot create' / 'snapshot restore <id> restored-computer'; POST /v1/computers can also 'Create a computer from an image or snapshot' (source.kind=snapshot), so new machines boot from it (fork/template). OpenAPI SnapshotResponse has capture_scope enum [filesystem, computer] and runtime_state enum [absent, included], suggesting some snapshots include runtime (memory) state, but docs do not say so explicitly; computer-host README says 'disk snapshots'. Linux only (not on macOS computers).

harness_api.quote:
computer claude-login	Install Claude Code credentials onto a computer.
computer codex-login	Install Codex credentials onto a computer.
harness_api.note: Only credential installation for Claude Code/Codex plus a generic exec API and ConnectRPC process/PTY gateway. The full public OpenAPI spec has no agent/prompt/conversation endpoints. The separate open-source computer-harness repo runs a local browser 'Agent UI' with Claude, Codex and OpenCode, but that is a UI, not an API to drive them.

egress_allowlist.quote: Network speeds up to ~1 Gb/s down and ~1.2 Gb/s up over shared NAT.
egress_allowlist.note: No egress/firewall/network settings anywhere in docs or the complete OpenAPI spec (CreateComputerRequest has additionalProperties:false and no network field). Host uses nftables internally (computer-host README) but no user-facing control.

egress_http_rules.note: No egress controls of any kind in the public API.

ingress_rules.quote: Ports are public by default: the resulting URL is reachable from the open internet without an access session, which is what you want for webhooks and other unauthenticated callers. Pass --private to require an access session instead
ingress_rules.note: Per-port publish with visibility public|private; only published ports are exposed; private ports need an access session (short-lived token). Share links for browser/VNC with expiry and revocation. SSH via short-lived certificates. No IP allowlists.

guest_firewall.note: Firecracker microVM with its own kernel (computer-kernels repo); default user is node, exec accepts a user field; root access not explicitly documented.

secret_proxy.quote: computer claude-login	Install Claude Code credentials onto a computer.
secret_proxy.note: Credentials are copied into the machine (claude-login/codex-login, exec env vars, S3 keys passed to FUSE mount). No credential-injecting proxy documented.

volume_attach.quote: The current limits are 2-64 GiB RAM in 1 GiB steps and 5-250 GiB storage in 1 GiB steps.
volume_attach.note: Storage is a single resizable disk (actions/resize); no block/network volume resource in the complete OpenAPI spec. Only BYO-bucket FUSE mounts (see volume_shared).

volume_shared.note: First-party FUSE mount API (POST /v1/computers/{id}/mounts) of your own R2/S3/GCS/WebDAV bucket with read_only flag and vfs_cache_mode; several computers can mount the same bucket (read-write or read-only). Bucket credentials are passed into the mount (not proxied). Only in OpenAPI/SDK (ComputerMountsClient), not in prose docs; Linux only.

docker_inside.quote: CONFIG_CGROUPS=y / CONFIG_NAMESPACES=y / CONFIG_USER_NS=y / CONFIG_NET_NS=y / CONFIG_OVERLAY_FS=y / CONFIG_BRIDGE=y / CONFIG_VETH=y / CONFIG_NF_NAT=y
docker_inside.note: derived: the Firecracker guest kernel config ships cgroups, namespaces, overlayfs, bridge/veth networking and NAT — everything Docker needs — and the default image gives the 'node' user passwordless sudo/root. Docker itself is not preinstalled in the computer-guest Dockerfile, but nothing in the kernel or exec API blocks installing and running it.

nested_virt.quote: CONFIG_KVM_GUEST=y (no CONFIG_KVM=y / CONFIG_KVM_INTEL / CONFIG_KVM_AMD entries in the guest kernel config)
nested_virt.note: derived: the guest kernel enables paravirtualized KVM-guest support only; it does not build the KVM hypervisor module, so /dev/kvm is not available inside a Linux computer. macOS computers themselves run as a full QEMU/KVM VM on the host, not exposed as nested virt to the guest.

computer_use.quote: Agent Computer runs on computer-host, a Firecracker-based hypervisor... Every computer boots from the computer-guest image ... pre-configured with browser access, SSH
computer_use.note: not offered: the public API/CLI/SDK expose exec, files, ports, VNC/browser connect and snapshots, but no screenshot+click 'computer use' style action API. VNC (computer open --vnc) gives raw remote-desktop pixels/input only, driven by a human or a third-party computer-use agent, not a first-party API.

anti_bot.quote: Cloud computer infrastructure for ai agents, provisioned on bare metal hosts.
anti_bot.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Agent Computer is generic VM/desktop infrastructure (Firecracker microVMs plus a browser/desktop image); no stealth/fingerprinting-evasion feature is documented anywhere in the docs, API, or repos.

captcha_solving.quote: Cloud computer infrastructure for ai agents, provisioned on bare metal hosts.
captcha_solving.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. No CAPTCHA-solving endpoint or mention exists in the OpenAPI spec, CLI, or docs.

egress_ip_type.quote: Network speeds up to ~1 Gb/s down and ~1.2 Gb/s up over shared NAT.
egress_ip_type.note: Computers share host NAT egress on bare-metal datacenter hosts; no residential/mobile proxy product is offered and no static IP is documented (public_ipv4_available: false).

snapshot.quote: SnapshotResponse: capture_scope enum [filesystem, computer], runtime_state enum [absent, included]
snapshot.note: The computer-host README calls these 'disk snapshots' and the schema's default/documented path is filesystem capture; runtime_state has an 'included' option suggesting memory/process state can sometimes be captured, but no docs page confirms restoring a snapshot resumes running processes, so this is modelled conservatively as filesystem-only ('fs'), medium confidence. Linux only, not available on macOS computers.

snapshot_auto.quote: Use snapshots when you want a saved computer state you can return to later. computer snapshot create my-computer
snapshot_auto.note: not offered: snapshots are explicitly user-triggered via CLI/API (computer snapshot create / POST /v1/computers/<id>/snapshots); no documented automatic snapshot-on-stop/sleep behavior.

fork_running.quote: createSnapshot: 'Queue snapshot creation.' / createComputer: 'Create a computer from an image or snapshot.'
fork_running.note: Cloning a computer goes through create-snapshot-then-restore-from-snapshot, an asynchronous two-step process (snapshot creation is queued, 202 accepted); there is no single-call clone-while-running endpoint, so a running machine is not cloned instantaneously without any pause in its own lifecycle.

memory_snapshot_fork.note: No docs text confirms that restoring a snapshot resumes running processes/memory state (the modelled 'snapshot' field above is fs-only); forking is therefore not documented to preserve running memory state.

wake_on_request.quote: POST /v1/computers/<id>/actions/start — Start a stopped computer. POST /v1/computers/<id>/actions/ensure-ready — Start the computer if it isn't already running or starting.
wake_on_request.note: not offered: starting a stopped computer is an explicit API/CLI action; there is no documented mechanism where an inbound request to a published port automatically wakes a stopped computer.

auto_stop_idle.quote: Pay only for what you use: runtime CPU/RAM, hot storage, and cold storage are billed separately.
auto_stop_idle.note: not offered: computer state transitions (provisioning/starting/running/updating/stopping/stopped) are driven only by explicit start/stop/ensure-ready API calls; no idle-timeout auto-stop is documented.

agent_harnesses.quote: RUN npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code @openai/codex && npm cache clean --force
agent_harnesses.note: The default computer-guest image ships Claude Code and Codex CLIs preinstalled, and the CLI has dedicated 'computer claude-login' / 'computer codex-login' commands to install credentials for them.

own_agent_api.note: not offered: the public API is purely infrastructure (create/exec/files/ports/snapshots/mounts); there is no first-party task/browser/computer-use agent to drive via API.

mcp_server.quote: computer-guest, torch, computer-host, computer-harness, computer-kernels, computer-nix, computer-cli
mcp_server.note: not offered: no MCP-server repo/package is published by AgentComputerAI, and no MCP mention appears anywhere in the docs, llms.txt, or OpenAPI spec.

lang_python.note: Preinstalled in the default computer-guest image.

lang_node.note: Node.js 22 is preinstalled in the default computer-guest image.

static_egress_ip.quote: Network speeds up to ~1 Gb/s down and ~1.2 Gb/s up over shared NAT.
static_egress_ip.note: not offered: computers egress through shared host NAT; no static/dedicated egress IP option is documented, and public_ipv4 is explicitly unavailable.

gpu.quote: Pay-as-you-go pricing based on actual resource usage: CPU Time, Memory, Hot Storage, Cold Storage
gpu.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Pricing and the computer-images/size-preset API only cover CPU/RAM/storage on Firecracker microVMs (plus a macOS QEMU/KVM VM); no GPU SKU, image, or size preset exists.

windows.quote: CreateComputerRequest.platform enum [linux, macos]; ComputerImageResponse.platform enum [linux, macos]
windows.note: The platform enum in the public API only supports linux and macos; there is no Windows option anywhere in the API, CLI, or docs.

arm64.note: The Firecracker guest kernel build target is x86_64 only; the configs/ directory contains only an x86_64 subfolder.

self_host.note: not offered as a customer-run product: Agent Computer is sold as a hosted API/CLI service (computer-host/computer-kernels are the provider's own internal infra, not a packaged product customers deploy); Enterprise mentions 'private infrastructure options' via sales, not a documented self-hosting path.

open_source.quote: computer-cli - Public mirror of the Agent Computer CLI
open_source.note: Only the CLI (public mirror), the guest image, host README, kernel configs, and a Nix harness are open-sourced; the core control-plane/API service itself is closed-source, so the product as a whole is not open source.

eu_data_residency.quote: ComputerCapacityCheckRequest/Response have no region field; no /v1/regions endpoint exists
eu_data_residency.note: not offered: the public API has no region parameter or region-listing endpoint anywhere, and no region/EU mention appears in the docs; the product is described only as bare-metal hosts with no location selection.

max_session_h.quote: computer power-off my-computer  Stop a computer without deleting its stored state. computer power-on my-computer  Recreate a computer runtime against the same stored state.
max_session_h.note: Computers are billed by actual runtime and only stop when the user calls stop/power-off (or deletes); no maximum session-length limit is documented anywhere in the docs, pricing, or API.

image_oci.note: Computers can only be created from the provider's own curated computer-images catalog (image_id references a listed ComputerImageResponse, platform enum linux|macos) or from a snapshot of an existing computer. The full OpenAPI spec (additionalProperties:false throughout) has no endpoint to upload/register a custom Docker or OCI image, no registry/tag/digest field, and no 'docker'/'oci' terms anywhere. So bringing your own container/OCI image is not supported; confirms the card's false.

public_ipv4.quote: Network speeds up to ~1 Gb/s down and ~1.2 Gb/s up over shared NAT.
public_ipv4.note: Docs explicitly describe networking as 'shared NAT', i.e. computers do not get a dedicated public IPv4 address; inbound access is instead via provider-issued hostnames for published ports (docs/computers: 'Ports are public by default: the resulting URL is reachable from the open internet ... derive the final URL from the computer handle and the published port name'), not a raw IP. The complete OpenAPI spec (CreateComputerRequest/ComputerResponse) has no ip/ipv4/address field. Confirms the card's false.

live_resize.quote: POST /v1/computers/{computer_id}/actions/resize — "Queue a computer resize." (202 "Computer resize accepted.")
live_resize.note: resize is a computer action (like exec/ports/snapshots) taken against an existing, running computer_id rather than a create-time-only parameter, and docs/computers lists 'resize' among the Linux-only live actions available on a running computer (alongside exec, mounts, published ports). It's an async/queued action (202 accepted) so it may briefly interrupt the guest rather than being instantaneous, but the machine itself is not recreated/deleted.

byoc.quote: Enterprise ... Custom computer capacity policies, Team billing and managed rollout support, Private infrastructure options, Priority operational support
byoc.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Agent Computer describes itself as "Cloud computer infrastructure for ai agents, provisioned on bare metal hosts" (its own Firecracker fleet on computer-host); the only enterprise mention is vague sales-gated 'private infrastructure options', with no documentation anywhere (docs, OpenAPI, GitHub org) of deploying the managed control plane into a customer's own AWS/GCP/Azure account.
